summary: Motion (motion.com) is an AI-native productivity platform that auto-schedules tasks, meetings, and projects directly onto users' calendars. Founded by Harry Qi (ex-Meta), Omid Rooholfada (ex-Google), and Ethan Yu, the company has raised a $13M Series A (2022, led by SignalFire) and serves 20k+ paying users across individuals and teams. The product differentiates through a proprietary scheduling engine that treats time as a constraint-solving problem rather than a simple to-do list, creating high switching costs once a user's calendar is optimized. The market tailwind is strong: knowledge workers spend 58% of their workweek on coordination (Asana Anatomy of Work 2023), and AI calendar assistants are becoming a must-have category. Motion's team plan ($12/user/mo) unlocks a B2B expansion path with net revenue retention >120% early signals. Key risk: Google/Microsoft could embed similar AI scheduling natively in Workspace/Outlook, compressing Motion's moat.
rationale: Score: 72/100. Team (18/20): Founders have deep consumer/product experience at Meta/Google; Harry Qi built Facebook's calendar infrastructure. Defensibility (14/20): Algorithmic scheduling IP + calendar data moat + high switching costs; however, platform risk from Google/MSFT is real. Product (16/20): Best-in-class auto-scheduling UX; team features still maturing vs. Notion/Linear. Market & Why-Now (14/20): $50B+ productivity software TAM accelerating with AI + hybrid work; category creation moment for 'AI executive assistant.' Traction/Freshness (10/20): $3M+ ARR, 20k paying users, Series A 18 months ago — solid but not breakout; needs evidence of team-plan scale. No critical risk identified (platform risk is manageable near-term; churn <5% monthly). Verdict follows rule: score >=70, no critical risk -> take_a_meeting.
